mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a budget planner and a 50/30/20 budget calculator?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 50/30/20 calculator splits one take-home figure into needs, wants and savings. A budget planner lists every income source and expense line so you see exactly where money goes, then compares the totals with the 50/30/20 guide.

mainEntity.name: How do I turn weekly or biweekly pay into a monthly budget amount?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply weekly pay by 52 and divide by 12, or biweekly pay by 26 and divide by 12. A $1,000 weekly paycheck is $4,333.33 a month, and $1,000 every two weeks is $2,166.67. The planner does this for you when you pick the pay frequency.

mainEntity.name: What is a savings rate and how is it calculated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your savings rate is the money you save or invest divided by your income. Saving $850 from $4,500 a month is a savings rate of 18.9%.

mainEntity.name: What is the possible savings rate?

acceptedAnswer.text: It adds the money left over after all planned spending to your planned savings, then divides by income. If you save $850 and have $510 unassigned from $4,500, the possible savings rate is (850 + 510) ÷ 4,500 = 30.2%.

mainEntity.name: Which expenses should I count as needs, wants or savings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Needs are costs you must pay, such as rent, utilities, groceries, insurance and minimum debt payments. Wants are costs you could pause, such as dining out and subscriptions. Savings include your emergency fund, retirement contributions and extra debt payments.

mainEntity.name: What if my spending is higher than my income?

acceptedAnswer.text: The planner shows a shortfall. Look at the wants first, since they are the easiest to cut, then review needs such as housing and transport. Even a small gap adds up over a year.

mainEntity.name: Should I enter income before or after tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: Enter income after tax, the amount that reaches your bank account. Taxes taken out of your paycheck are not part of your spending budget.

mainEntity.name: How do I include irregular costs such as annual insurance or holidays?

acceptedAnswer.text: Enter the full yearly cost and set the frequency to Yearly. The planner spreads it as one twelfth each month, so a $1,200 trip counts as $100 a month.
